fixes.summary: Replace the scale-free rule gap <= 0.1*E_dense (global_error.rs:715) with a three-part admissibility criterion evaluated in CASE-tolerance weights w = atol_case + rtol_case*|y_ref|. (A) Per-arm reference-aware budget: with E_a = max_i WRMS(y_a(t_i)-y_ref(t_i)) and reference uncertainty U in the same weights, the true error satisfies |E_a* - E_a| <= U (triangle inequality), so arm a in {clipped,dense} is WithinBudget iff E_a + U <= B, ExceedsBudget iff E_a - U > B, and ReferenceDominated (undecidable) otherwise; B is a predeclared constant in tolerance units (proposed B = 10; on the E-03 n=96 data the verdicts are invariant for any B in [4.3, 16.9]: non-semilinear dense rows max 4.2, semilinear 17/53/207, scipy Radau max 1.6). (B) The clipped-vs-dense gap G is demoted from a gate to an integrity assertion plus recorded diagnostic: y_c - y_d = (y_c - y_ref) - (y_d - y_ref) gives G <= E_c + E_d <= 2*max(E_c,E_d) identically for ANY y_ref, so a bound with constant >= 2 can only fail on grid/weight misalignment (hard error), while any constant < 1 re-creates the unattainable rule (E-03: scipy Radau itself violates 0.1 in 17/18 pairs, median ratio 1.29). (C) Output-policy sensitivity is gated by a same-step-sequence comparison: for every grid point t_i inside an accepted dense step [t_k, t_k+h_k], delta_i = WRMS(y_dense(t_i) - S(t_k,y_k; t_i-t_k)) where S is one hard-stop step restarted from the same accepted state; both are local approximations from the same y_k, so delta_i <= (interpolant local defect) + (sub-step local error) and the gate is max_i delta_i <= 2.0 tolerance units, reference-free and reachable by any solver whose local control holds. Row status order becomes ReferenceDominated -> GlobalErrorExceedsBudget{arm} -> InterpolantDominated -> Pass, issued under a NEW campaign/protocol id (the committed ab8fbcd records and their frozen 0.1 rule stay immutable as historical nonpassing evidence). Failure modes still caught: solver globally outside tolerance on either arm (the semilinear rows, previously masked by the policy verdict); broken dense interpolant coefficients/theta mapping (delta blows up, independent of reference); hard-stop landing corruption (clipped arm fails A, or delta fails); inadequate reference (undecidable band); metric pipeline misalignment (triangle assertion). Not caught: error common to both arms that stays below B.

fixes.summary: adaptive_next_step_after_attempt (adaptive.rs:279-282) returns the pre-clip requested_h unchanged after every accepted clipped step and discards the error sample, so the controller's request is frozen between rejections. Keep the 'remember the pre-clip h' intent but let the sample update it: compute candidate = trial_h * factor(error); if the sample is informative (trial_h/requested_h >= 0.5) record it in PI history and, when it predicts rejection of the remembered request (error*(requested_h/trial_h)^q > 1), lower the request to clamp(candidate, trial_h, requested_h); in every other case return max(requested_h, candidate), so a sliver landing (trial << requested, error at roundoff floor) can never collapse h. Because integrate.rs:757-761 and all dense hard-stop loops (dense_output_v2.rs:379-484, 572-715, 811-899, 943-1024, 1181-1251) and radau.rs:645-691 share this helper, one change covers every observed/hard-stop lane. Protocol consequence that the controller change alone does NOT remove: an arm that hard-stops at every point of a uniform 101-point grid is by construction an h <= span/100 integrator (output.rs:281-282 returns (to_next, true) whenever base > to_next), so in the 26/54 zero-rejection rows the clipped arm will still take exactly 100 steps; the campaign must therefore rename that arm 'hard-stop-every-output (h <= grid spacing)' and stop presenting it as an adaptive run, or restrict hard stops to physical breakpoints via OutputSamplingPlan::new(output, hard_stops). Adjacent observation while editing: the non-clipped branch calls record_acceptance(error) BEFORE propose_factor (adaptive.rs:283-284), so under ControllerKind::Pi `previous` equals the current error and the PI law degenerates to safety*error^(-0.3/q); the campaign uses the integral controller so its records are unaffected, but the ordering should be fixed in the same patch.

fixes.summary: Report every campaign metric in two declared bases: the existing tight reference basis (absolute 1e-10, relative 1e-8; kept for continuity and checksum identity) and a case-tolerance basis built from spec.atol/spec.rtol anchored on the same reference states, with a basis id stored next to each number. The freeze threshold (campaign 1024-1026) and the holdout comparison (1084-1085) must be computed in case-tolerance units, or per-rtol stratum, because a single max over 54 tight-basis rows is dominated by rtol=1e-4 rows (semilinear 3.8e5) and would admit an rtol=1e-8 holdout row at ~1e4 times its own tolerance. Reference uncertainty must be converted with the same weights: when atol_case/rtol_case == 1e-10/1e-8 the weights are exactly proportional and every WRMS scales by 1e-8/rtol_case (the conversion the audit used); otherwise recompute from raw states and bound U_case <= U_tight * max_j(w_tight_j / w_case_j). The loader check at numerical_reference.rs:811-815 stays as is (it pins the reference artifact policy, not the evaluation basis).

fixes.summary: Give the semilinear exceedance its own row status and an attribution arm instead of letting the output-policy verdict consume it. Under the replacement criterion the three n=96 semilinear dense rows (17, 53, 207 case-tolerance units; scipy Radau 0.24, 1.6, 0.47 on the same problems) classify as GlobalErrorExceedsBudget, which is the solver-relevant result. Add a diagnostic-only third arm per row, 'dense-tight-inner', identical to the dense arm except that the per-stage residual forcing heuristic (sequential.rs:366-370, rejection at 507-513) is replaced by the fixed fallback inner tolerance (rtol 1e-10 / atol 1e-12 already in the campaign config), and record R_inner = E_dense / E_dense_tight_inner; R_inner > 2 attributes the excess to inexact stage solves, R_inner ~ 1 sends the investigation to W-method/non-autonomous order reduction, to be settled by a fixed-h convergence-order study (h, h/2, h/4) on the same family. The mechanism is NOT established by the audit (no exact-stage run was possible) and the ledger must say so; what is established is that the embedded estimator btilde*K (sequential.rs:583-585) is built from the same inexactly solved stages, so error common to all stages is invisible to it, and that the dense interpolant is not the cause (E-03c ratio 1.00-1.02 on semilinear rows). Correct the finding's wording when it is transcribed: the dense arm did reject 3-8 steps per row, so 'accepts every step' must read 'every accepted step has embedded norm <= 1'. Any change to the forcing rule itself belongs to group G2 and should consume R_inner as its acceptance metric.
